html:
The Year of Africa is the name given to 1960, when seventeen African countries became independent. It was the peak of the decolonisation of the continent.

The new states fell into a few groups:

  • Fourteen former French colonies, among them Senegal, Mali, Ivory Coast, Niger, Chad, Madagascar and Cameroon. Most kept close links with France, including the CFA franc.
  • The Belgian Congo, which became independent on 30 June. Within days it fell into the Congo Crisis.
  • Nigeria, the most populous, independent from Britain on 1 October.
  • Somalia, formed by joining British and Italian Somaliland.
  • Togo, a former trust territory.

The new members changed the United Nations. In December 1960 its General Assembly passed a declaration calling for a quick end to colonial rule everywhere.

The same year showed the limits of change. In February the British prime minister Harold Macmillan warned white South Africa of a "wind of change" in his speech in Cape Town. In March police killed protesters at Sharpeville, and armed resistance to apartheid began soon after. Portugal kept its colonies until 1975. The bar of independent African states grows most sharply at this point.
sum: The Year of Africa is the name given to 1960, when seventeen African countries became independent. It was the peak of the decolonisation of the continent.
